title: Android TabWidget: letter widths
purpose: Check that wrap-content tabs account for the actual widths of different letters rather than only their number.
changes: Wrap-content Android text now uses the renderer's glyph advances. This XML example compares three narrow i letters with three wide W letters.
steps: Turn on Glyph width example. The middle WWW tab should be much wider than either iii tab, even though both labels have three letters.
Tap WWW to select it, then turn on Right-to-left layout and check the tabs again.
Choose OK if it looks and behaves as described, or Reject with details and your device.
expected: The WWW tab is visibly wider than the iii tabs, the wider letters receive more space, and selection and RTL work.
limits: The example uses ASCII glyph advances supplied by the web renderer. Bhoo sums individual glyph advances, so kerning is not reproduced. Non-ASCII shaping, Android fonts and device visual parity remain unverified.
validation: The complete libbhoo Rust test suite and 156 XML importer tests passed. A glyph-specific Rust test covers narrow, wide and multiline text.
A 320 × 850 browser test compared tab widths with the sum of renderer glyph advances and checked selection and RTL.
